data.title: Front-end Developer at AxiomQ
data.subtitle: August 2026 – Present
data.excerpt: Where I am now. AxiomQ is a software company out of Novi Sad with a second office in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, building eLearning platforms, enterprise tools, and business process software for clients in the US and Europe. I work on the front end in React. The product itself sits under a strict NDA, so that is as much as I can say about it.

data.title: Front-end Developer at NQode
data.subtitle: April 2024 – May 2026
data.excerpt: An agency in Novi Sad, and three clients through it: one of several front-end teams on a greenhouse platform, the only front-end developer on a prop trading app, then two months of animation-heavy marketing sites.

sections.label: Clients
sections.title: One agency, three clients.
sections.intro: Most of my time at NQode went to client work. Each of the three clients needed something different from me.

items.name: Source AG
items.summary: A greenhouse-intelligence platform for commercial growers. Several front-end teams build it, and I worked in one of them.
did: A Next.js front end that reads from a GraphQL API.
Some work on the Nest.js back end as well.

shot.caption: Source · public site
shot.alt: Source's public home page: AI solutions for smarter greenhouse cultivation, with photos of tomatoes on the vine

items.name: BrightFunded
items.summary: A prop trading firm. I was the only front-end developer on its client app and owned the UI end to end.
did: About twelve screens, built and maintained by me.
The whole component library underneath them, in Angular.
The hardest part was the purchase flow, which is heavily customised.

shot.caption: BrightFunded · public site
shot.alt: BrightFunded's public home page on a dark background: 'We fund traders up to 400K' above a Get Funded button and a row of trader payouts

items.name: Owow
items.summary: A digital agency. I spent two months building animation-heavy marketing sites with them.

shot.caption: Owow · public site
shot.alt: Owow's own site on black: selected work shown as large device mockups with project names and service tags

sections.label: Libraries
sections.title: Two component libraries, end to end.
sections.intro: Both times I built the whole library, not a few components inside someone else's.

points.body: The component library under the internal tools NQode builds for its own use.
The component library under the client app's twelve or so screens, written in Angular.

data.title: Front-end Developer at EPAM Systems
data.subtitle: February 2022 – April 2024
data.excerpt: Two years on one live product: Meridianbet, a sports betting and casino site. I worked across its Angular front end, from UI polish and the Win&Go casino game to live data arriving over WebSockets.

index.label: The product
index.note: One client, live the whole time

index.label: The work
index.note: From UI polish to the WebSocket feed

index.label: The team
index.note: Fourteen people, four of them in QA

sections.label: The product
sections.title: One client, live the whole time.
sections.lede: Meridianbet was the only client I worked for at EPAM. Its sports betting and casino site stayed live while we shipped into it.

shot.caption: Meridianbet · home with live odds
shot.alt: Meridianbet's home page: casino promotions across the top, featured matches with odds, a live football table, and the bet slip on the right

points.body: UI polish across the site, plus the everyday features and fixes that kept it moving.
Front-end work on Win&Go, one of the site's casino games.
Live data reached the UI over WebSockets. I worked on that path as well as on the screens it fed.

sections.label: The team
sections.title: Four testers for nine developers.
body: A large QA team tested our work by hand and with automation. The checks were strict and the deadlines were tight.

data.title: Front-end Developer at Codeplicity
data.subtitle: February 2021 – February 2022
data.excerpt: My first job: a seven-person agency in Novi Sad. I wrote JavaScript and Sass for client sites built on PHP templates.

points.body: Everyone in one office, designers and back-end developers included.
Client sites rendered on PHP. My JavaScript and Sass went into those templates.
Projects ran locally in Vagrant boxes. I used them; someone else set them up.
